manifest.title: A Constrained Physics-Guided Method for Wellbore Alignment
manifest.description: Technical explanation of the protected-parent architecture, HGRG, role-separated corrections, and geological-component validation.

blocks.body: # A Constrained Physics-Guided Method for Wellbore Alignment

## Technical summary

A stable learned trajectory anchors the pipeline. Particle filtering and GeoHMM propose an alignment, HGRG sizes the move, and Meta-State adds regional structure. Boundary continuity and local shape are handled by two small overlays. The same target-free geological graph governs folds, holdout assignment, and bootstrap units. Sequential gain was positive in all ten saved outer folds across two disjoint 160-well panels.

## Results across both geological panels

The sequential method improved pooled RMSE in all four saved contracts. The direction was consistent across two disjoint panels and every outer fold. All contracts use training seed 20260806.

The chart compares each candidate only with its matching incumbent and contract. Primary and Complement panels should not be added together. The Complement holdout is also the key caveat: pooled RMSE improved by 0.6587 ft while worst-10% component CVaR increased slightly, so average improvement did not imply universal safety.

## Outer-fold gains

All ten outer-fold gains are positive. The smallest gain was 0.2666 ft and the largest was 1.1221 ft.

## Sequential method

```text
observable inputs
      |
      +--> learned parent
      +--> particle paths --------+
      +--> GeoHMM alignment ------+--> HGRG bounded move
      +--> training-only region --+         |
                                             v
                                      Meta-State trend
                                             |
                                             v
                                      boundary continuity
                                             |
                                             v
                                      centered local shape
```

Datum, regional trend, boundary hand-off, and local shape use separate movement budgets.

## HGRG

HGRG forms a PF/GeoHMM bridge and measures its displacement from the protected parent. PF/GeoHMM dispersion is normalized by the requested movement. The projection of the Ridge residual onto that movement provides a directional check. High relative disagreement or opposition from Ridge shrinks the coefficient. The accepted move ramps in over 250 ft and obeys a 2.5-ft well RMS budget and 10-ft row cap.

## Scope and metric definitions

TVT is the geological target. The latent structural coordinate is U = TVT + Z, which separates geological motion from known borehole motion. Pooled RMSE weights rows equally. Macro-component RMSE weights connected geological components equally. Harmed-well rate is the share of wells whose candidate RMSE exceeds the incumbent. Worst-10% component CVaR is the mean RMSE of the worst ceiling of 10% of components. Outer OOF means every development prediction came from a model fitted without its component. Run holdout means complete components were excluded until the final development refit.

## Limitations

The saved contracts use one model-training seed. Component bootstrap draws measure sensitivity to represented geology. PF and GeoHMM spread is not calibrated as a prediction interval. The source data do not establish a coordinate reference system, which limits interpretation of spatial thresholds. The historical 9.091 submission depends on external artifacts and cannot be reconstructed byte for byte from this repository alone.

## Next experiments

1. Register at least three independent refits under one frozen split.
2. Estimate expert second moments inside inner folds before enabling empirical constrained GLS.
3. Predeclare a leave-region-out or externally defined type-well-family contract.
4. Calibrate uncertainty at geological-component level.
5. Require pooled and macro-component gains without a material tail-risk regression.

## Further questions

Can disagreement be converted into calibrated abstention rather than only movement shrinkage? Does an empirical correlated-error model transfer across regions? Which observable signatures distinguish a true geological regime change from a gamma-ray outlier? These questions require new frozen evidence rather than additional tuning on the existing panels.

constraint_ledger.failure_mode: All experts can agree on the same wrong alignment
Sparse or biased regional anchors can mislead
A real dip change can invalidate tangent continuation
Clipping can alter exact post-projection mean
